content.comment_body: I've been searching online for software that can flash a [product_name] device without needing the [product_name] IDE. We want to update the firmware on a [product_name] at the site without using the full [product_name] package. Is there any tool that allows this without giving the customer access to change the program?

Hello, Upgrading the firmware isn't possible. If you are referring to updating the program to a newer version, you can use a memory cartridge to store the program, then transfer it via a memory card using the same type of [product_name] device. Sending the card will cause the device to start with the new program. For version [version_no], a memory card (MMC) can be used to store the application. Regards, [user_name]

Sorry, I forgot to mention the [product_name] version; we're using [version_no]. Yes, I meant updating the program. The memory card solution sounds perfect. Does the [product_name] automatically run the program from the memory card if it's inserted?
Hi, Yes, you can load the program from the memory card to the [product_name] either manually or automatically during power cycles. Hope this helps.
Thanks very much everyone, this seems like a suitable solution.

analysis.insight_summary: The main question is about updating the program on a [product_name] device on-site without relying on the full [product_name] IDE, seeking a straightforward method that prevents customers from modifying the application. The discussion clarifies the difference between firmware upgrades and program updates, and confirms that using a memory card for program transfer is an effective solution for easy updates.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a simple and secure way to update the program on a [product_name] device without allowing the client access to modify the application themselves.
